verdict.rationale: Render documents a Workflows product: Python and TypeScript SDKs let you define workflow tasks in code with `task()`, trigger runs and chain task runs. Render also markets these as reliable background processes 'without wiring up queues, workers, and retry logic.' Durability and long-running behavior are asserted only in marketing copy, without detailed docs or hands-on confirmation. Missing for 10: documented durability/state-persistence semantics, explicit long-running execution limits, detailed retry configuration docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy durable, long-running workflows as code without manually wiring queues and retries

citations.quote: Deploy reliable agents and background processes at scale, without wiring up queues, workers, and retry logic.
The Render SDK for TypeScript provides support for: - Defining workflow tasks - Triggering runs of those tasks from your other TypeScript code
The Render SDK for Python provides support for: - Defining workflow tasks - Triggering runs of those tasks from your other Python code
Use `task()` to register a provided function (`func`) as a workflow task with the specified `options`.
Chaining additional task runs from within a task function
